candidates.summary: No test feeds a duplicated key, in pubkeys or in excluded, although Ethereum sync committees carry duplicates and the native's per-entry (multiset) subtraction is what makes them verify
candidates.failure_scenario: Ethereum's get_next_sync_committee_indices returns 'the sync committee indices, with possible duplicates' (consensus-specs electra/beacon-chain.md:831), and process_sync_aggregate builds the non-participant list per position (altair/beacon-chain.md:644-646), so a member sampled twice and absent twice must be subtracted twice. Today the native does that: committee {pk1,pk2,pk2,pk3}, excluded [pk2,pk2], sig s1+s3 verifies; excluded [pk2] does not. Every in-tree committee is random distinct keys (signers(), committee()) or three/four fixed distinct keys (.gno vectors), so a refactor that deduplicates keys (a map cache of decompressed keys, a 'reject duplicate excluded' guard) keeps every test green while every update from a committee with a duplicated absent member fails to verify.

candidates.angle: topic: aggregate not a plain sum / equivalence claim
candidates.summary: The identity check on aggregate refuses a committee whose keys sum to the identity before excluded is applied, so Excluding answers false where FastAggregateVerify over the same signers answers true, against the equivalence bls12381.go:67-69 states
candidates.failure_scenario: Committee {pk, -pk} (one operator holding sk and -sk, each key with a valid PoP): aggregate is the identity, excluded [-pk], sig = sk*H(m). FastAggregateVerify([pk], m, sig) is true; FastAggregateVerifyExcluding(identity, [-pk], m, sig) is false at line 86. Ethereum's own process_sync_aggregate subtracts from bytes48_to_G1(aggregate_pubkey) with no identity check on it (altair/beacon-chain.md:650-655). Only a false rejection, no forgery, and only for a committee summing to the identity; verifyAggregate already refuses an identity signers' key, so dropping '|| agg.IsInfinity()' loses no check.

candidates.angle: topic: duplicates in excluded (doc vs native)
candidates.summary: The Gno doc reads excluded as a set ('the members ... that are not in excluded', 'every key in excluded is a member') while the native subtracts per entry, so a realm that deduplicates excluded rejects valid signatures from a committee with a duplicated absent member
candidates.failure_scenario: Ethereum committee {pk1,pk2,pk2,pk3}, pk2 absent at both positions. A realm following the doc literally lists pk2 once (it is 'in excluded'); the native returns false for the honest s1+s3. It needs one entry per absent position, as process_sync_aggregate builds it (altair/beacon-chain.md:644-646). Stating 'one entry per absent committee position, duplicates included' at .gno:43-46/50-52 closes it.
